card: Prevents Bitcoin Core from aborting on an assertion failure if SQLite database creation fails during legacy BDB wallet migration. Instead of deleting the legacy file upfront and asserting success, the migration creates the SQLite database under a temporary filename and only replaces the legacy file after successful completion. This fixes node crashes on network filesystems that do not support SQLite locking, as well as on full disks or permission errors.
evidence: Author encountered a node abort with assertion failure: './wallet/wallet.cpp:3868: bool wallet::CWallet::MigrateToSQLite(bilingual_str&): Assertion `new_db` failed.' on a CIFS mount due to SQLite locking failure ('fcntl ... EACCES').
problem: When migrating a legacy BDB wallet to SQLite, CWallet::MigrateToSQLite() deletes the legacy database file before creating the new SQLite database and asserts that creation succeeds. If creation fails—such as on network filesystems lacking POSIX lock support, on full disks, or with permission errors—the node crashes with an assertion failure and leaves behind an empty wallet.dat with only the .legacy.bak backup.

risk.why: Bugs in the wallet migration sequence or file cleanup logic could cause wallet database corruption or data loss.

scope_notes: Diff is missing from the record, but metadata indicates changes across 6 files including migration logic and new test coverage.
summary: Handle SQLite database creation failures gracefully during wallet migration instead of aborting on an assertion. Write migration records to a temporary SQLite database alongside the legacy BDB file, swapping it into place and removing the old file only after migration succeeds.
